message.content:
### What “CPU Usage” Means  

**CPU usage** (sometimes called *processor utilisation* or *load*) measures how much work your computer’s central processing units (CPUs) are doing at any given moment.  
It is usually expressed as a percentage:

| Value | Interpretation |
|-------|----------------|
| **0 %** | No active processes – idle state |
| **1–20 %** | Light background activity (e.g., system daemons, minimal apps) |
| **21–50 %** | Moderate workload – typical for everyday tasks (web browsing, office software) |
| **51–80 %** | Heavy multitasking / moderate‑intensity applications (video editing, gaming) |
| **81–100 %** | Near‑maximum load – often indicates bottlenecks or runaway processes |

> ⚠️ A high overall average doesn’t always mean something is wrong; some workloads legitimately keep CPUs busy (renderers, scientific simulations, servers).

---

## How to Check CPU Usage

Below are quick ways to view real‑time CPU utilisation on common platforms. If you’d like me to fetch live data from your own machine, let me know which OS you’re running and I’ll guide you through executing the right command.

| Platform | Tool/Command | Typical Output |
|----------|--------------|---------------|
| **Windows** | `Ctrl+Shift+Esc` → Task Manager → Performance tab → CPU graph | Shows % Processor Time, number of cores, threads, etc. |
| | PowerShell: `Get-Counter '\Processor(_Total)\% Processor Time' -Continuous` | Streams continuous values. |
| | Command Prompt: `wmic cpu get LoadPercentage` | One line showing total load. |
| **macOS** | Activity Monitor → CPU column | Percent each process uses + aggregate bar. |
| | Terminal: `top -l 1 -n 0 | grep "%Cpu"` | Snapshot of CPU stats. |
| | `ps aux --sort=-pcpu | head` | Top consumers. |
| **Linux** | `htop` or `top` | Interactive display of all processes & per‑core percentages. |
| | `/proc/stat` parsing (`cat /proc/loadavg`) | System load averages over 1/5/15 min. |
| | `mpstat -P ALL 1` (from sysstat package) | Per‑core statistics. |

---

## Interpreting Common Metrics

| Metric | Where You See It | Meaning |
|--------|------------------|---------|
| `% Idle Time` | In many utilities | Portion of time CPU was completely free. |
| `% User`, `% Nice`, `% Sys`, `% IRQ`, `% SoftIRQ` | Linux `vmstat` or `sar` | Breakdown of CPU time spent in various modes. |
| **Load Average** | `uptime`, `w`, `top` | Number of runnable/processes queued over last 1/5/15 minutes. Not a direct % but useful trend indicator. |
| **Per‑Core Utilisation** | htop, mpstat, macOS Activity Monitor | Helps spot hot spots when one core runs near 100 % while others stay low. |

---

## When High CPU Is a Problem

| Symptom | Likely Cause | Quick Fix Ideas |
|---------|-------------|-----------------|
| PC feels sluggish, programs lag | Single thread stuck in tight loop | Identify offending process via task manager/top; kill/restart or update driver/software. |
| Fan noise spikes constantly | Sustained >70 % across most cores | Clean vents, ensure proper airflow, consider better cooling. |
| Battery drains fast on laptops | Background services consuming CPU | Disable unnecessary startup items, adjust power plan to balanced/performance mode. |
| Server shows high load avg vs actual traffic | Inefficient code, memory leaks, missing indexes | Profile application, add caching, scale horizontally. |

---

## Sample Commands (if you need to automate)

```bash
# On Linux: show top 5 CPU hogs once
ps -eo pid,%cpu,comm --no-headers | sort -k2nr | head -n 5

# On macOS: same thing
ps -Ao pid,pcpu,comm --sort=-pcpu | head -n 5

# On Windows PowerShell:
(Get-WmiObject win32_processor | Measure-Object -Property LoadPercentage -Average).Average
```

If you tell me your OS and whether you prefer GUI or CLI, I can tailor instructions—or even help you write a small script that logs CPU usage over time!
